title: How long is each piece of the wooden block?
description: A wooden block four metres long is cut into five equal pieces. Four is divided by five by multiplying both numbers by two, the same way as in the book's example, and the answer is checked by putting the pieces back together.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the length is smaller than the number of pieces, divide the length by the number of pieces and the answer is a decimal less than one. Watch for children who divide five by four.

source: A 4 m long wooden block has to be cut into 5 pieces of equal length. What is the length of each piece?
video_script.why: The child has learnt to multiply both numbers by the same amount before dividing, and now uses it to share four metres among five pieces.
video_script.substitution: the book's own wooden block of four metres cut into five equal pieces
video_script.anchor: A wooden block four metres long, cut into five pieces of equal length
video_script.payoff_line: The length of each piece is now known.
maths_rules: size check: 5 pieces of 1 m would need 5 m, so each piece is shorter than 1 m
video_script.design: One idea: share the length by dividing it by the number of pieces, and multiply both numbers by the same amount to make the divisor ten. Assumes the book's example of multiplying both numbers by ten. The block stays all video; the decimal appears only on the answer beat.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, multiply both numbers by two, the same way as in the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Four times two is eight, and five times two is ten.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>This makes four divided by five the same as eight divided by ten.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, eight divided by ten is eight over ten.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>That is eight tenths of a metre.

beats.on_screen: Check: 5 pieces × 8 tenths = 40 tenths = 4 m, the length of the block

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, put the answer back in the question. Five pieces of eight tenths are laid end to end.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Five times eight tenths is forty tenths.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Forty tenths is four metres, the length of the block.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 8 tenths of a metre = 0.8 m; each piece is 0.8 m long
